memory_update.text: MYRG should be tracked as an underfollowed AI power-enablement candidate because company materials explicitly connect AI data-center growth to interconnections, substations, C&I electrical work, and T&D opportunities.

PLPC is a lower-attention small-cap grid-hardware candidate; direct AI exposure is unproven, but its transmission, distribution, substation, and communications infrastructure products map to the grid-upgrade chokepoint.

PRIM provides a mid-cap utility-services and power-delivery route into AI data-center power constraints, with explicit disclosures around power generation, data centers, critical infrastructure, and PayneCrest data-center services exposure.

POWL is larger and more discovered than ideal for the underfollowed lane, but its medium-voltage switchgear and behind-the-meter data-center order evidence make it a high-relevance benchmark for smaller electrical equipment peers.

For this node, the best Layer 1B discovery map is not only utilities or nuclear power; it is the enabling stack of electrical contractors, substations, switchgear, utility construction labor, line hardware, and behind-the-meter integration.

Further passes should search for sub-$1B transformer/switchgear suppliers, private-to-public customer dependencies, regional utilities with data-center load concentration, and micro-cap speculative exceptions only if direct order evidence exists.

node: Grid interconnection, transmission, substations, utility power procurement and baseload availability
summary: Layer 1B expands the underfollowed discovery lane for the AI power-availability chokepoint. The strongest non-mega-cap public mappings found in this pass are specialty electrical contractors, medium-voltage switchgear/control suppliers, transmission/substation hardware vendors, and utility-services contractors. The common thread is not AI model ownership but the physical gating steps needed before AI data-center capacity can be energized: interconnection studies, substations, transmission upgrades, switchgear, utility construction labor, and behind-the-meter power integration.
